guardian_issue:
  id: "WASI-9"
  component: "The digest the docs publish is not the digest the release carries"
  module: "CHANGELOG.md:117, docs/runbook.md:90, wasi/ci/check-release-asset.sh"
  status: ready
  priority: high
  in_scope:
    - "the docs name the released artifact's digest, and the platform it belongs to"
    - "a guard that compares the recorded digest with the release page"
  out_of_scope:
    - "cross-platform reproducibility (a Linux build and a macOS build are different bytes)"
  acceptance_criteria:
    - "the digest in the docs equals `gh release view v1.14.3 --json assets`"
    - "a stale recorded digest fails a check, not a reviewer"
  validators: [docs, ci, canonical]

```

# WASI-9 · Three digests, one tag — and the documented one is neither

`v1.14.3` was cut from `c8d162e1` and published. Measured after it went live:

| where | digest | size |
|---|---|---|
| **the release page** (`package-wasi`, ubuntu-latest) | **`ab77bb82…`** | **1 899 431 B** |
| `CHANGELOG.md:117` and `docs/runbook.md:90` | `b0ed0ee6…` | 1 897 095 B |
| a rebuild of the tag on this machine (macOS, same toolchain pin) | `0cfacf43…` | 1 899 660 B |

The page and its `.sha256` agree with each other (I downloaded both: `shasum -a 256` → `ab77bb82…`, and `sha256sum -c` passes), and `verify-release-asset` passed because `--expect` is the artifact *this run* built — so the release is internally sound. The documentation is not.

`CHANGELOG.md:117` says:

> `a314672c` builds `7414f8df…` (1,896,910 bytes); `main` at this tag builds `b0ed0ee6…` (1,897,095 bytes), because four batches of engine code landed in between. Verified by rebuilding `a314672c` in a worktree with the pinned toolchain: byte-identical to the recorded digest, so the build is reproducible and the difference is code, not compiler.

The first half is true — I reproduced `7414f8df…` from `a314672c` myself, twice, in a different directory. The second half is **not**: `b0ed0ee6…` is not the release asset and does not reproduce from the tag on this machine either. It is a number that denotes no artifact anyone can obtain.

`docs/runbook.md:90` is where it does damage: *"`main` at `v1.14.3` builds `b0ed0ee6…`, so a vendor pinned to the former…"* — a vendor following that sentence pins a digest its download will not have.

## Why this is the class this repo keeps finding

- **A digest must denote one artifact.** Three numbers for one tag is the same defect as a version number that denotes two builds.
- **A measurement has a context.** A Linux CI build and a macOS build are legitimately different bytes; the number is meaningless without the platform and toolchain it came from. The release is reproducible *per toolchain*, which is the property worth claiming.
- **A recorded number that nothing compares is a wish.** `check-release-asset.sh` already reads the page and takes `--expect`; nothing reads `CHANGELOG.md` or the runbook.

## End state

- `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/runbook.md` name **`ab77bb82…`, 1 899 431 bytes, built on ubuntu-latest by `package-wasi` at `c8d162e1`** — the number a download will produce.
- The sentence about `b0ed0ee6…` is either removed or replaced with the measurement that produced it *and its context*; a number whose provenance cannot be restated should not be in the record.
- A check in the release job: after `github-release`, compare the page's digest with any digest the docs record for that tag, and fail on a mismatch naming both. The release already runs `check-release-asset.sh`; this is one more comparison in a job that now has the facts in hand.
- The general rule, stated once: **a digest in the docs is the release page's digest, quoted.**

## Acceptance

| # | Criterion | Command | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | the docs match the page | `gh release view v1.14.3 --json assets` vs `grep -n 'ab77bb82\|b0ed0ee6' CHANGELOG.md docs/runbook.md` | the same digest, once |
| 2 | the context is stated | the same lines | platform + toolchain + commit |
| 3 | a stale number fails | change the recorded digest in a scratch copy, run the check | refused, naming both numbers |
| 4 | the release still passes | `bash wasi/ci/check-release-asset.sh v1.14.3` | green |
title: docs(wasi): the digest the CHANGELOG and runbook publish is not the digest the release carries

  module: "engine/.pi/scripts/validate-adr-references.sh (:202-250, :148)"
  status: ready
  priority: low
  in_scope:
    - "the descriptive count names citation sites, not recorded labels"
    - "the self-test summary distinguishes seeds that must be accepted from seeds that must be refused"
  out_of_scope:
    - "the rules themselves, which bite"
  acceptance_criteria:
    - "each printed count's noun matches what was counted"
    - "the self-test summary equals the accept/reject counts it printed above"
  validators: [tests, canonical]

```

# ADR-3 · The guard's two summary lines are counts of the wrong noun

Found while validating #1505. The rules work — `65 labelled citations resolve` is right, and the seeds bite. Two lines around them do not describe what ran, in a guard whose purpose is to stop exactly that.

## 1. "3 descriptive label(s) are recorded" — there are 2

```
$ grep -cvE '^\s*#|^\s*$' engine/.pi/architecture/adr-citation-labels.tsv
2
$ bash engine/.pi/scripts/validate-adr-references.sh | tail -1
✅ ADR references: 65 labelled citation(s) resolve to the subject they name, 3 descriptive label(s) are recorded
```

`descriptive` is a list of **citation sites** (`validate-adr-references.sh:226,246`): one tuple per citation that used a recorded label. `ADR-013 (write-deny boundary)` is cited twice (ADR-018, ADR-019) and `ADR-016` once, so 3 sites use 2 labels. The printed noun says labels.

The report repeated it — *"3 descriptive labels recorded"* — which is how a count of the wrong noun becomes a fact about the wrong file. The fix is one word: `3 citation(s) use 2 recorded label(s)`, or simply `2 descriptive label(s) recorded, used at 3 citation(s)`.

## 2. "every seed was rejected" — four of the ten cases assert acceptance

```
$ bash engine/.pi/scripts/validate-adr-references.sh --self-test | tail -1
✅ every seed was rejected and the control case passed
```

The ten cases in `--self-test` are four `pass` (`control: a matching label passes`, `a recorded descriptive label passes`, `a § section that exists passes`, `a cited filename that exists passes`), five `fail`, and one `malformed`. A summary that says "every seed was rejected" is false about four of them, and the report inherited it as *"9 seeds rejected"*.

This is the same class the guard was built to catch, one level up: the *rules* check that a label names its target; nothing checks that the guard's own output names its own cases. Given the file is the reference for how to state a count, the summary should be derived (`${accepted} accepted, ${refused} refused`) rather than typed.

While in the file: `:236` carries `if True:` around the whole body — dead since the rule was written. Not a defect, but in a guard it is the kind of line that makes the next reader wonder what was removed.

## Acceptance

| # | Criterion | Command | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | the count matches the file | `bash engine/.pi/scripts/validate-adr-references.sh` | the label count equals `grep -cv '^\s*#' adr-citation-labels.tsv` |
| 2 | citations are counted separately | same | a second number, labelled citations |
| 3 | the summary is derived | `--self-test` | `N accepted, M refused`, matching the printed lines |
| 4 | the seed | delete a `pass` case from the self-test | criterion 1's count still matches (no hardcoded number) |
title: fix(guard): the ADR reference guard's summary lines count the wrong noun and call accepted seeds rejected
